changelog.note: v2.4.0 (Oct 12): place_option_order gains stop and stop-limit order types, GTC time in force and a stop_price parameter; locates tools now say they are not available in paper trading. Tool set otherwise unchanged. Source: https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server/releases/tag/v2.4.0

tools.name: Interactive Brokers AI Integration (MCP)
tools.order_approval_safety: hosted at api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp-public; IBKR login, single-account authorization; order instructions require IBKR approval (you review and submit each order; the Connector also supports two-leg option strategies). Separately, IBKR Autonomous Trading (announced Oct 21, 2026) lets eligible clients authorize connected AI to execute supported orders without approving each one, only inside a dedicated AI Partition funded with cash from the parent account; IBKR's AI integrations page says it is planned for eligible clients of IBKR LLC, Australia, Singapore and U.K., limited to individual, non-margin accounts that first execute at least 10 trades of $100 or more over two weeks in Review & Approve mode, and to stocks, ETFs and listed equity, ETF and index options with market, limit, stop and stop-limit orders (Day, Overnight or Overnight + Day); penny stocks, complex leveraged products, fractional shares, short sales and option strategies that need margin are excluded (IBKR, Oct 28); IBKR says an eligibility test is coming as an alternative to the trade requirement and plans order-frequency, maximum-order-size and minimum-account-value limits; access can be revoked in Client Portal; AI Integration is not available in India or Japan
tools.pricing_free_tier: no additional cost (per IBKR's AI integrations page); needs an IBKR account
tools.order_gating_note: You approve each order, unless you opt in to IBKR Autonomous Trading (eligible clients)

changelog.note: Pricing filled in: IBKR's AI integrations page says there are no additional costs. Source: https://www.interactivebrokers.com/en/trading/ai-integrations.php

IBKR officially announced Autonomous Trading: eligible clients can let connected AI submit supported orders without per-order approval, inside a dedicated, separately funded AI Partition. Source: https://www.interactivebrokers.com/en/general/about/mediaRelations/10-21-26.php

Autonomous Trading eligibility corrected: IBKR's page sets rule-based eligibility (individual non-margin accounts after 10+ Review & Approve trades of $100+ over two weeks) and calls the service planned. Source: https://www.interactivebrokers.com/en/trading/ai-integrations.php

IBKR's Oct 28 Traders' Toolbox article on Autonomous Trading: the AI Partition can trade stocks, ETFs and listed equity, ETF and index options with market, limit, stop and stop-limit orders (Day, Overnight, Overnight + Day); penny stocks, complex leveraged products, fractional shares, short sales and margin option strategies are excluded; an eligibility test and more user-set limits are planned. Source: https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/traders-insight/ibkr-toolbox/traders-toolbox-ai-order-placement-is-here/

tools.name: Longbridge MCP
tools.live_vs_paper: live trading tools (place/modify/cancel); paper trading accounts work too, except on Longbridge US accounts, which have no paper account
tools.order_approval_safety: hosted; vendor advises start read-only, enable trading after scope config; 160+ tools; two-step order flow: submit, replace and cancel orders, fund orders (submit/cancel) and grid orders first return a code that the agent sends back to execute; the code is single-use, expires in 10 minutes and applies only to that exact order, and since v0.14.0 (Oct 16) it covers every field that changes what is traded; DCA and multi-leg orders still execute on the first call; since v0.15.0 (Oct 26) the account and order tools also work on Longbridge US accounts
tools.pricing_free_tier: Trading, account, fundamentals and news APIs are free; only real-time quote permissions (e.g. HK LV2, OPRA) are paid add-ons
tools.order_gating_note: Can place orders; vendor advises starting read-only

changelog.note: v0.14.0 (Oct 16): the two-step order code now covers every traded field (order type, time in force, triggers, expiry), so a code from one previewed order can no longer place a different one. DCA and multi-leg orders still execute on the first call. Source: https://github.com/longbridge/longbridge-mcp/pull/171
Clarified from Longbridge's docs: the confirmation code also gates cancel_order and fund order submit/cancel, is single use and expires in 10 minutes. Source: https://open.longbridge.com/docs/mcp

v0.15.0 (Oct 26): balance, position, cash-flow and order tools now work on Longbridge US accounts, plus a new fx_rate tool (public ECB reference rates). The MCP docs now say Longbridge US accounts have no paper trading account, so agents on a US account trade live from the start. Sources: https://github.com/longbridge/longbridge-mcp/releases/tag/v0.15.0 and https://open.longbridge.com/docs/mcp

tools.name: Webull Cloud MCP Server
tools.live_vs_paper: live: creates order instructions (stocks, options, futures, crypto, event contracts, algo) that you confirm in the Webull app/desktop; plus account data, order history, market data
tools.order_approval_safety: hosted at api.webull.com/mcp; OAuth login; you pick which accounts and capability groups to authorize; every order instruction requires confirmation in the Webull APP/Desktop and can be revoked; Webull Canada clients can connect too (announced Oct 27, 2026, rollout to eligible accounts by early November), with the same rule that nothing executes until you review and confirm the order on Webull
tools.pricing_free_tier: Webull says there is no extra charge for API access; trading fees match the app and market data subscriptions are bought separately
tools.order_gating_note: Creates order instructions you confirm in the app

changelog.note: Webull's MCP docs now list screeners, market sentiment, unusual activity, news, fundamentals, financial statements and institution/insider data, and say MCP market data permissions match your Webull app subscriptions. No safety change. Source: https://developer.webull.com/apis/docs/AI-friendly-Resources/mcp

Webull Securities (Canada) announced on Oct 27, 2026 that Canadian clients can connect their Webull accounts to ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Grok over MCP; an AI assistant can prepare an order but nothing is executed until the investor reviews and confirms it on Webull. Rollout to all eligible accounts is expected by early November. No safety change. Source: https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/webull-canada-introduces-ai-powered-investing-that-lets-you-trade-using-plain-language-876060210.html

Oct 26: Webull's API changelog says the Cloud MCP Server added 24 data tools (news, community posts, option market data and contracts, institutional and insider data, macroeconomic data, market sentiment, unusual activity and NOII). Order instructions still need confirmation in the Webull app or desktop. Source: https://developer.webull.com/apis/docs/changelog/

tools.name: tastytrade MCP Server
tools.live_vs_paper: live by default (connects to production unless TASTYTRADE_ENV=sandbox); sandbox available (no market data, resets every 24 hours)
tools.order_approval_safety: order submit/edit tools require a single-use confirmation token from a dry_run tool (valid 60s, bound to request hash); self-hosted (no tastytrade-hosted endpoint); TASTYTRADE_READ_ONLY=1 blocks write tools; MAX_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD caps order value (default $50,000); other destructive tools, including order cancels, act on the first call; the API cannot access any money movement actions or endpoints, so the MCP is limited to reading and order placement if trade permissions are granted (direct email confirmation from tastytrade API support, Connor, api.support@tastytrade.com, Oct 23, 2026). Open source: tastytrade publishes the server source for self-hosting at https://github.com/tastytrade/tastytrade-mcp under the MIT License (LICENSE file, Copyright (c) 2026 tastytrade). Peter, lead Product Manager for tastytrade's MCP, pointed us to it by email on 2026-10-26 (api.support@tastytrade.com)
tools.pricing_free_tier: tastytrade: $0 stock/ETF commissions, $1 per contract to open options ($10 max per leg); no subscription
tools.rate_limits: tastytrade's per-endpoint limits plus a global cap of 50 requests per second in the server
tools.order_gating_note: Single-use confirmation token from a dry run

changelog.note: tastytrade publishes the MCP server source for self-hosting at https://github.com/tastytrade/tastytrade-mcp under the MIT License (LICENSE file, Copyright (c) 2026 tastytrade). Peter, lead Product Manager for tastytrade's MCP, pointed us to it by email on 2026-10-26 (api.support@tastytrade.com). The open source or audited safety input is now 10. The safety score is 100/100 (was 90/100).

incidents.title: Binance said its initial investigation suggests an attacker used a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop to reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions, and that it found no evidence of a wallet private key compromise. It suspended all deposits and withdrawals as a precaution, is working with law enforcement, says it will cover all losses and will publish a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete.

Polymarket said one of its third-party providers was compromised, affecting users of its international platform Polymarket.com; it put the exchange in cancel-only mode, paused relayer actions and halted trading for about an hour (18:05-19:05 UTC, Trading API included), fixed the issue, referred it to law enforcement and says anyone impacted will be made whole.

Predict.fun said a small number of users had unauthorized transfers from their wallets totaling about 400,000 USDT. Its preliminary investigation points to its API documentation site, hosted by a third-party provider, being compromised; the docs site is offline until the investigation ends. Predict.fun says it will fully reimburse affected users and publish a post-mortem.

Coinbase said a security incident at its third-party analytics vendor Amplitude exposed contact information for a 'small subset' of customers. It said its systems showed no unauthorized access and customer funds remain safe.

Bloom said an attacker exploited a remote code execution vulnerability in a third-party module and drained 49 wallet addresses belonging to 9 users, about 9,408 SOL ($947,000); it says no private keys were compromised and took all systems offline as a precaution. Later the same day Bloom said all 9,408 SOL had been refunded to the 9 users. No detailed post-mortem yet.

Keystone's full statement: an attacker used a vulnerability in a third-party monitoring tool on its website (detected October 20) to take 25,964 buyer records, 12,873 unpaid checkout records and the WebAuth key used to check that a device is genuine. Keystone says recovery phrases and private keys were not involved; the risk is counterfeit devices passing the authenticity check. It is destroying 18,835 inventory devices with the old key and asks anyone who received a device after October 20 to follow its verification guidance.

Foundation (Passport hardware wallet) said phishing emails were sent from its own domains after attackers got into part of its backend through a vulnerability in a self-hosted application and likely accessed its customer support inbox; some emails included customers' mailing addresses or phone numbers. Foundation says Passport devices and funds are not compromised, it cut off the attackers' email access within about 10 minutes and revoked all API keys. Never enter seed words anywhere except on the Passport itself.

Initia said a bug in MoveVM script caching let an attacker credit themselves unbacked WETH, iUSD and USDC and bridge about $2.7M out (via LayerZero and CCTP, swapped to 1,135.52 ETH) before it halted the L1 and its rollups; it said no native INIT was minted and that a fix was being written and audited.

Keystone said a third party pulled customer shipping data (names, contact details, shipping addresses, items bought and prices) from its website store via the Shopify API, detected October 20 and confirmed October 23; it said payment details, recovery phrases, private keys and wallet passwords were not exposed, and warned of scammers posing as Keystone with refunds or replacement devices.

Electrum released 4.8.3 as a security update; press reports of its advisory say earlier versions let a malicious Electrum server plant a fake pending payment so that a later fee bump (RBF) paid the attacker, and that users of trusted servers were not exposed. Update to 4.8.3 or later.

GMO Internet shut down its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud Windows VPS service (popular for running FX trading bots on MT4/MT5) after finding programs planted by a third party on customer servers on October 20; up to 26,739 servers may be affected, customers reported unauthorized trades from trading logins stored on the servers, and GMO says it refused a ransom demand. It is paying every customer ¥5,000 and will compensate confirmed losses from unauthorized trades. From a device you don't trade on, change your broker and platform passwords, end sessions and turn on 2FA.

Railway disclosed that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and obtained the decrypted contents of some of them; it told users to immediately roll all environment variables and API keys stored in Railway and paused all deployments while it investigates.

Microsoft reported that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth app abuse in a ConnectWise cloud backup supply-chain compromise aimed at hundreds of organizations.

Node.js security releases v22.23.4, v24.22.1 and v26.12.1 fix ten vulnerabilities, including a high-severity Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that permits remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497) in the 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines.

Qubic said an attacker drained 1,404 Qubic wallets (about 2.94 trillion QU) between 23:42 UTC on October 17 and 01:26 UTC on October 18 because some wallet seeds were generated with insufficient randomness (seeds made on iPhone or iPad browsers or Mac Safari before October 18, 2026, or in the Qubic iOS app before July 2025); it says the protocol itself was not at fault. Computors halted the network; on October 20 Qubic said the recovery was approved and opened a reclaim platform (weak-seed-reclaim.qubic.org, claims until May 1, 2027).

Ledger said hardware wallets sold through the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden implants that read the screen during setup, captured the 24-word recovery phrase and sent it out over LTE through an embedded eSIM; attackers then drained funds (drains on October 9, disclosed October 13). Ledger says the implant leaves the Secure Element intact, so tampered devices may still pass its authenticity check, and that all confirmed thefts involve CryptoBilis devices.

MetaMask said it was responding to a security incident in part of its infrastructure, in its non-custodial staking operations, and exited affected Ethereum staking validators (including its Lido validators) as a precaution. It said it found no immediate threat to MetaMask wallets and did not disclose the cause.

An intruder at Brevo, Trezor's newsletter provider, exported 347,149 marketing email contacts and sent Trezor subscribers a fake 'STM32 entropy vulnerability' email asking for wallet backups. Trezor said no Trezor product, wallet or account system was affected.

confirmed_via: https://trojan.com (links x.com/TrojanOnSolana, docs.trojan.com, and its 'Telegram Bot' button to trojanonsolana.com)

https://docs.trojanonsolana.com/ (links t.me/odysseus_trojanbot, which also appears on trojanonsolana.com/links)
official.notes: @solana_trojanbot is the main trading bot. trojanonsolana.com/links also lists backup bots @achilles_trojanbot, @menelaus_trojanbot, @diomedes_trojanbot, @paris_trojanbot, @helenus_trojanbot, @hector_trojanbot, @agamemnon_trojanbot and @nestor_trojanbot (vendor-listed only; not separately double-confirmed). @trojantrading is a support group, not a bot; the vendor pages also show t.me/trojan and t.me/trojan_on_solana as support links, inconsistently. The bot usernames are confirmed only from Trojan's own pages (two separate vendor pages reached from the confirmed official domain), with no independent third-party match found. trojan.com is the newer web terminal (trojan.com/terminal). Third-party directories disagree: DappRadar lists trojanbot.work and Solana Compass lists trojan.app and @TrojanTrading. No Trojan-owned page links to any of these, so do not treat them as official.

custody.note: Trojan's terms say it is 'not a custodian' and that your Trading Wallet is provided by a 'third-party wallet provider via an SDK'; the site shows Privy as a partner, but the terms don't name the provider. You can export the private key from wallet settings ('Export Private Keys') and import a wallet with a private key. How the Telegram bot itself stores the keys of the wallets it creates is not documented on any page we could access.

can_move_funds_out.note: Withdrawals from the Wallets page: you enter any receiving address and click Withdraw.

checks.worst_case: Trading runs from a hot wallet that Trojan's bot or its wallet provider can sign for. If your Telegram account, that wallet's private key, or Trojan's systems are compromised, everything in the wallet can be withdrawn to any address, and Trojan's terms say it is not liable.
safe_setup: Open the bot only from the links on trojanonsolana.com/links or trojan.com (main bot @solana_trojanbot), never from DMs, ads or search results
Use a fresh Trojan wallet and keep in it only what you are trading; regularly withdraw profits to a wallet that never touches the bot
Never paste the exported private key anywhere else, and turn on Telegram 2-step verification to protect the account that controls the bot

collects: Identifiers: IP address, device ID, advertising IDs (IDFA, Google Advertising ID) and IMEI
Device and browser details, including browser fingerprint data such as fonts, plugins and screen resolution
Your wallet addresses and transaction data (transaction records kept up to 6 years)
Geolocation, usage data, search queries and your communications with Trojan
Trading wallet keys and encrypted seed phrases, if you authorise storing them for signing
Website and app: cookies, pixels and similar tools from unnamed analytics and advertising partners
privacy.can_see: Trojan's privacy policy (operator Odyssia Labs) says it may store your trading wallet's keys and encrypted seed, if you authorise it, solely to sign your transactions, and it names Telegram and third-party wallet SDKs as services it relies on. That means Trojan sees every trade and the wallet's balance, and its records tie your wallet addresses to your IP address and device IDs. Trades are also public on the Solana blockchain, so anyone who knows your bot wallet's address can follow it.

Transaction data for your trades, kept up to 5 years after your account ends (Maestro says it deletes a terminated wallet's keys right away, or within 3 months after a permanent suspension)
Personal information if Maestro asks you to verify your identity, kept while you use the service and for 5 years after

privacy.can_see: Maestro's bot creates (or imports) your trading wallet and keeps its private key, AES-encrypted, on its servers so it can sign every trade you send in Telegram. So Maestro sees each trade and everything in that wallet, linked to your Telegram account. Trades are also public on each chain Maestro trades on (Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain, Base and others), so anyone who knows your bot wallet's address can follow it. incidents.amount: More than $750,000 at the time of writing (SC Media, 2018-12-28)

https://3commas.io/security (vendor 'official channels' list: 3commas.io, app.3commas.io, help.3commas.io, feedback.3commas.io, status.3commas.io; emails support@3commas.io, security@3commas.io)

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.threecommas.client.global (listing '3Commas: Crypto Trading Tools', developer 3C Trade Tech Ltd, email support@3commas.io, points to 3commas.io, 10K+ downloads)
https://coinbureau.com/review/3commas-review (third-party review links 3commas.io/exchanges, /pricing, /refund, /security)
official.notes: Only 3commas.io and the Google Play app are double-confirmed (vendor site plus an independent listing or review). The vendor site and its security page also list app.3commas.io, help.3commas.io, feedback.3commas.io, status.3commas.io and trade.3commas.io (docs, terms) but we found no independent second source for each, so only the registered domain is listed. App Store id6446649413 is linked from the vendor homepage but apps.apple.com could not be fetched, so it is left out. X: the vendor footer links x.com/3commas_io, while Kraken's 3Commas partner page (kraken.com/gb/pro/3commas) links x.com/3Commas, a different handle, and x.com could not be fetched, so no X handle is listed. Telegram: the vendor footer uses bit.ly redirect links and t.me/Community_3Commas (single source), so none is listed. No GitHub found. 3Commas says it provides software only; trading is done on your exchange. Legal entities seen: 3C Trade Tech Ltd (Google Play) and 3Commas Technologies OU (named in a 2023 US class action), not reconciled here. 3Commas says its support email is support@3commas.io.

custody.note: Your coins stay in your account on the exchange you connect (Binance, Kraken, Coinbase, etc.). 3Commas holds the API keys and secrets that let its bots place orders on that account, stored in its 'Sign Center', which it describes as 'a secure API key storage isolated at both infrastructure and access levels'. 3Commas says it 'provides software only' and 'has zero access to withdraw or transfer fiat or cryptocurrencies'. The Dec 2022 leak showed those stored keys are a target.

can_move_funds_out.note: Only if the key is set up as 3Commas' docs say: 3Commas guides tell you to 'provide TRADING access only and DISABLE the withdrawal option', and Kraken's 3Commas page says withdrawal permission is not required. A key with withdrawal enabled could move funds if leaked. Even a trade-only key can place bad orders on your balance, which is how the 2022 thefts worked (per Bitsgap and Coin Bureau).

api_keys.note: 3Commas' key guide says to give TRADING access only and disable withdrawals. It lists per-exchange permissions: Binance (Spot & Margin Trading and Futures, restrict to trusted IPs), OKX (Trade), Bybit (Read-Write plus Unified Trading), Kraken, KuCoin (Spot Trading), Gate (Read and Write), Bitget (Read-write), Coinbase (Trade). It recommends using the whitelisted 3Commas IP addresses shown under My Exchanges > Add exchange (Gate keys without IP binding last only 90 days, and the guide tells KuCoin users to set IP restriction to 'No'). Another 3Commas help page says to use API keys only for 3Commas and not link the same exchange account to another trading service. Its security page says 'The IP whitelist can be used to restrict the API key to certain IP addresses'. Hyperliquid keys expire about six months after connecting.

incidents.title: Proposed US class action (Freeman et al. v. 3Commas Technologies OU, No. 4:23-cv-00101) alleges 3Commas did not encrypt stored API data, that the breach exposed at least 100,000 consumers and led to nearly $22 million in theft. These are allegations, not findings.
incidents.outcome: No ruling or settlement reported on the source page

incidents.title: API data leak: an anonymous poster published a sample of ~100,000 API keys. After first denying a leak and pointing to phishing, 3Commas confirmed on 2022-12-28 that 'the data in the files is true' and asked Binance, KuCoin and other exchanges to revoke all keys connected to 3Commas. Binance's CEO had urged users to disable keys. The FBI was reported to be investigating. 3Commas says it found no evidence of an insider, and the attackers claimed an employee sold the data.
incidents.amount: Traders reported ~$22M stolen (Decrypt); ZachXBT verified 44 victims / $14.8M (Decrypt); HAPI counted 86 victims / $27.3M (ForkLog)
incidents.outcome: 3Commas urged all users to reissue keys and promised no reimbursement until its investigation ended; HAPI says all exchanges have since disabled 3Commas keys. We found no source for any 3Commas compensation.

incidents.title: Phishing: lookalike sites captured users' exchange API keys, which were used to place ~20,000 unauthorized trades (DMG and other tokens) on several exchanges. 3Commas said its own systems were not breached at the time; the Dec 2022 leak later contradicted that.
incidents.outcome: FTX agreed a one-time ~$6M payout (Blockworks); 3Commas reported cloned sites for takedown

checks.worst_case: 3Commas holds API keys that can trade on your exchange account. If they leak (as ~100,000 did in Dec 2022) or are phished, attackers can place orders that drain your balance even without withdrawal rights, and 3Commas' terms cap its liability at the subscription price you paid. A key with withdrawal enabled could be emptied outright.
safe_setup: Open 3Commas only from 3commas.io (bookmark it) and turn on 2FA on both 3Commas and your exchange; never enter API keys on a site reached from ads, search results or DMs

Create the exchange API key with trading permission only and withdrawals disabled, restricted to the 3Commas IP addresses shown under My Exchanges > Add exchange (use a dedicated sub-account where your exchange supports it), and use the key only for 3Commas
Keep only the balance your bots need on that exchange account, and revoke the key at the exchange (not just in 3Commas) if you stop using it or suspect a leak

collects: Account: name, email, user ID, your 2FA key, login records, social handles, and profile details pulled from linked exchanges (ID, name, picture, email)
Exchange connections: the API key and secret for each exchange you link, plus your exchange account ID, deposit address and account status
Trades: date, time, amount, currency, order type and the order requests and responses exchanged with your exchange
Billing: email and country/postal code for card payments; wallet addresses and order IDs for crypto payments
Device: IP address, device type and IDs, OS, browser, ISP and city-level location (the policy says technical and usage data is kept 30 days)
Marketing and support: cookies, Google Analytics client ID, AppsFlyer and Affise attribution IDs, ad ID and UTM tags; the content of support messages
privacy.can_see: 3Commas keeps the API key and secret for every exchange you connect and uses them to place orders and read your exchange account, so it sees each order its bots place plus your account ID, deposit address and account status. Its policy says trade and account data can be kept up to 6 years after you stop using the service, and it doesn't say how stored API keys are protected. Trades on centralized exchanges aren't public on-chain, but the exchange also sees them.

breaches.summary: An anonymous poster published about 10,000 exchange API keys taken from 3Commas, claiming to hold 100,000. 3Commas confirmed the data was real: some users' API keys, secrets and passphrases had been disclosed, and it said no other data was taken as far as it knew. It asked Binance, Coinbase, KuCoin and other exchanges to revoke all 3Commas-linked keys, told users to reissue their keys, and reported the incident to law enforcement including the FBI. Leaked keys had been used for unauthorized trades since November 2022.

checks.name: Pionex
chains_or_assets: Multi-asset centralized exchange with built-in trading bots (spot, perpetual futures)

confirmed_via: https://www.pionex.com/blog/ (site footer links Telegram t.me/pionexen, Twitter, Reddit, Facebook; navigation links Discord)
https://coinmarketcap.com/exchanges/pionex (listing shows website pionex.com and Telegram t.me/pionexen)
https://apps.apple.com/hn/app/pionex-crypto-trading-bots/id1485348891 (App Store listing, seller BitUniverse CO., Limited, names www.pionex.com as its support site)
official.notes: X is left out because the sources disagree: the pionex.com footer links twitter.com/pionex_com, while CoinMarketCap lists twitter.com/pionex. We could not open either profile to check, so neither is listed. The iOS app (App Store id1485348891, seller BitUniverse CO., Limited) was not double-confirmed, because pionex.com did not link it in the pages we could fetch, so no app is listed. A GitHub org 'pionex-official' (pionex-open-api) appears in a third-party PyPI package page, but github.com could not be opened, so it is not listed. We could not open t.me/pionexen, so the group's size is unverified. Pionex.US (pionex.us, Telegram t.me/pionexus, X @PionexUS, iOS id1567213944) is a separate US-facing service with its own help center at intercom.help/pionexus; it is not covered by this entry. Pionex's own help center article 'How to Verify Official Pionex Channels & Avoid Scams' exists (listed at https://intercom.help/pionex/en/collections/19449950-getting-started), but its text could not be read here. Pionex's terms and its API-key permissions page could not be retrieved.

custody.note: Custodial exchange. Pionex says it keeps '100% reserve' and uses a Merkle tree plus an independent audit to show it; these are Pionex's own claims, and we did not find the audit report itself.

can_move_funds_out.note: Pionex says 'users can withdraw their coins at any time', and its help center has withdrawal guides for web and app. Trustpilot reviewers report withdrawals blocked during Pionex 'risk-control' reviews or until KYC is completed (user claims, not verified).

freeze_policy.note: Pionex's terms of use could not be retrieved, so the exact wording is not confirmed here. In public replies on Trustpilot, Pionex cites 'risk-control measures' when users report funds being unavailable, and reviewers describe trading and withdrawal restrictions followed by requests for personal and trading records.

api_keys.note: Pionex's API docs recommend setting up IP whitelisting along with the API key. Keys are created in the app or site under Account Settings, API Management (per CoinLedger's guide). The docs link to a separate 'API Key Permissions' page, which could not be retrieved, so whether keys have a withdrawal permission is not confirmed. Third-party guides say read-only keys are enough for tax and portfolio tools (CoinLedger, TradesViz).

incidents.title: Four US state regulators (Nebraska, North Carolina, Ohio, South Dakota) issued a consent order against Pionex Inc., the US entity, over failing to collect sender and beneficiary information on transfers above $3,000, information-security and record-keeping deficiencies, and operating before licensing in North Carolina and Ohio. Pionex did not admit wrongdoing.
incidents.outcome: Penalty plus two years of quarterly progress reports; no cease-and-desist

incidents.title: Pionex was attacked and suspended deposits and withdrawals while it repaired and upgraded its wallet functions (Wu Blockchain report, per CoinCodeCap). The article does not say how much was lost.
incidents.outcome: Per the article, Pionex said it had fully compensated affected users and would reopen deposits and withdrawals after the upgrade. We did not find Pionex's own notice.

incidents.title: Pattern of user complaints: Trustpilot shows a 2.5/5 score from 636 reviews (40% one-star). Themes include stuck withdrawals, trading and withdrawal restrictions after profitable trades or deposits, KYC-gated withdrawals, slow support and disputed compensation. Trustpilot does not verify reviews.
incidents.outcome: Pionex replies to most negative reviews, often citing risk-control measures; compensation limited to verified platform issues

checks.worst_case: Pionex holds your coins, so an exchange hack or insolvency, or an account restriction after a 'risk-control' review, could lock your balance and your running bots for an unknown time. The '100% reserve' claim is Pionex's own, and you would depend on Pionex's compensation decisions.
safe_setup: Type pionex.com yourself or use a bookmark; treat any Telegram or X DM, 'support' contact or giveaway as a scam, and join only the group linked from the site (t.me/pionexen)
Create API keys under Account Settings, API Management, bind each key to your bot's IP as the docs recommend, and enable only the permissions the bot needs
Keep only trading capital on Pionex and check your balance against its Merkle tree page; hold savings in your own wallet

collects: Identity checks: a copy of your government ID, date and place of birth, and tax or government ID numbers (the app asks for camera and photo access to upload them)
Contact: name, postal address, phone number, email, and what you send to support or in surveys
Money: account numbers, order amounts and digital wallet addresses; from other sources, credit history and sanctions-list status
Device: IP address, device and advertising IDs, device model, OS version, mobile carrier and ISP, and location
Website and app: cookies, pixel tags and local storage; unnamed analytics, identity-check, push-notification and support SDKs
privacy.can_see: Pionex holds your funds and its built-in bots run on Pionex itself, so it sees every order your bots place, plus your balances, deposits and withdrawal addresses. Pionex's privacy policy (effective 2026-10-22) names Marketa Trading Inc. as the operator of the Pionex app. Crypto deposits and withdrawals are also public on their blockchains.

checks.name: Bitsgap

confirmed_via: https://bitsgap.com (vendor homepage: links App Store id1407713776 and Google Play com.bitsgap.pwa, t.me/Bitsgap_news, YouTube, Facebook; meta tags name @Bitsgap; lists 16 exchanges: Aster, Binance, Bitfinex, Bitget, Coinbase Advanced, Crypto.com, EVEDEX, Gate.io, Gemini, HTX, Hyperliquid, Kraken, KuCoin, OKX, Poloniex, WhiteBIT)

https://bitsgap.com/helpdesk/article/10024820752540-How-to-follow-Bitsgap-updates-and-news (vendor list of official channels: twitter.com/Bitsgap, t.me/bitsgap, discord.com/invite/PwdsEsp4j8, reddit.com/r/Bitsgap, youtube.com/@bitsgap and others; says social profiles are 'not for customer support purposes'; support is support@bitsgap.com and in-platform chat)
https://apps.apple.com/app/id1407713776 ('Bitsgap: Crypto Trading Bots', seller Bitsgap Holding OÜ, privacy policy on bitsgap.com, v2.11.11)

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bitsgap.pwa ('Bitsgap: Crypto Trading Bots', developer Bitsgap Holding OU, developer website https://bitsgap.com/, email support@bitsgap.com, 50K+ downloads, updated 2026-08-12)
https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/tools/bitsgap-bitsgap-software-solutions (third-party directory: website bitsgap.com, X x.com/Bitsgap)
https://www.cbinsights.com/company/bitsgap (third-party: website bitsgap.com, founded 2017, HQ Tallinn, Estonia)
official.notes: Telegram is left out: the vendor gives two different channels (the site footer links t.me/Bitsgap_news, its 'follow Bitsgap' help article links t.me/bitsgap), and we found no independent source naming either. Discord is also inconsistent (vendor help article: discord.com/invite/PwdsEsp4j8; Quicknode: discord.gg/bitsgap) and is not a schema field. x.com could not be opened, so @Bitsgap rests on the vendor help article plus Quicknode. No GitHub found. Bitsgap says Telegram and Discord are for community only and do not provide support; support is support@bitsgap.com or the in-platform chat. Legal entities seen: Bitsgap Software Solutions FZCO (Dubai, named in the site footer and terms) and Bitsgap Holding OÜ (Estonia, the app-store publisher).

custody.note: Your coins stay in your own exchange accounts. Bitsgap says it 'connects through secure API keys only — we never move or hold your funds' and 'Your assets remain in your own exchange accounts at all times.' Bitsgap stores the API keys that let its bots trade; it says passwords and API keys are always encrypted (RSA 2048 per its help center). These are Bitsgap's own claims.

can_move_funds_out.note: Bitsgap refuses API keys that have withdrawal permission: its error-status article says 'The API key can't be used because the withdrawal permission is enabled', and its blog says such keys 'are rejected automatically on connection'. A trade-only key can still be misused to place bad trades on your balance; Bitsgap's blog warns a compromised key 'can still be misused within its trading scope, for instance to manipulate a thin market.'

freeze_policy.note: This covers the Bitsgap service, not your exchange funds. Bitsgap's terms let it suspend your account until the cause is fixed and suspend or end the service 'at any time without notice'. It caps its liability at the lower of AED 5,000 or the fees you paid over three months. The terms page shows no last-updated date.

api_keys.note: Bitsgap needs read (trade history, balances) and trading permission, and rejects keys with withdrawal enabled. For Binance its guide says to enable Reading, Spot & Margin Trading and (optionally) Futures. Binance, KuCoin, Kraken and Crypto.com require IP whitelisting for Bitsgap. You copy Bitsgap's trusted IP addresses from its Manual Replace or Fix window and add them to the key on the exchange; the addresses are not published in the help text. 'API Account Lock' blocks the same key from being used on more than one Bitsgap account and emails the account it is already linked to.

checks.worst_case: Bitsgap holds API keys that can trade on your exchange account. It refuses keys with withdrawal rights, so a leak or phishing attack cannot withdraw your coins directly, but an attacker with the key can place trades that drain value from your balance. Bitsgap's terms cap its liability at the lower of AED 5,000 or three months of fees.
safe_setup: Open Bitsgap only at bitsgap.com or its official apps (App Store id1407713776, Google Play com.bitsgap.pwa), and turn on 2FA or a FIDO2 security key for Bitsgap and your email, as Bitsgap's security page advises. Get support only via support@bitsgap.com or the in-platform chat, since Bitsgap says its socials are not support channels.

Create the exchange API key with read and trading permission only and withdrawals off (Bitsgap rejects keys with withdrawals enabled), and add Bitsgap's trusted IP addresses, copied from the Manual Replace or Fix window, to the key's whitelist on the exchange.

Re-check the key's permissions every time you connect it, as Bitsgap's blog recommends, and never paste API keys, passwords or seed phrases into Bitsgap's AI Chat; its terms forbid entering credentials there.

checks.name: OctoBot

confirmed_via: https://www.octobot.cloud (vendor site, 'Drakkar-Software © 2021-2026', 15 rue des halles, 75001 Paris: footer links github.com/Drakkar-Software/OctoBot, twitter.com/DrakkarsOctoBot, t.me/OctoBot_Project; community section links t.me/octobot_trading and discord.com/invite/vHkcb8W; links App Store id6502774175 and Google Play com.drakkarsoftware.octobotapp)

https://github.com/drakkar-software/octobot (Drakkar-Software/OctoBot, GPL-3.0, ~6.6k stars; About links www.octobot.cloud; README links t.me/octobot_trading, t.me/OctoBot_Project, x.com/DrakkarsOctoBot, App Store id6502774175)

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/octobot-crypto-investment/id6502774175 ('OctoBot: Crypto investment', seller DRAKKAR-SOFTWARE, developer website https://www.octobot.cloud, privacy policy octobot.cloud/privacy, v1.6.1)
https://pypi.org/project/octobot (package registry: homepage github.com/Drakkar-Software/OctoBot, author Drakkar-Software, latest stable 2.1.1 released 2026-03-29, 3.0.0 betas to 2026-10-08)
https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/octobot/index.html.md (DigitalOcean Marketplace listing links octobot.cloud guides and github.com/Drakkar-Software/OctoBot)
https://gainium.io/review/octobot (third-party review: GitHub github.com/Drakkar-Software/OctoBot, Telegram t.me/octobot_trading, Discord discord.com/invite/vHkcb8W)
official.notes: X is left out: @DrakkarsOctoBot appears only on vendor-controlled pages (octobot.cloud, the GitHub README and the vendor-written Docker Hub page) and x.com could not be opened. The news channel t.me/OctoBot_Project is also vendor-only, so it is left out; @octobot_trading is the community chat. Google Play is left out: octobot.cloud and AppBrain (https://www.appbrain.com/dev/Drakkar-Software/, 10,000+ installs, developer Drakkar-Software) both point to com.drakkarsoftware.octobotapp, but when we fetched that Play Store URL it returned a different app ('Gem Wallet'), so we could not confirm the listing. OctoBot is open-source software you can self-host (Docker image drakkarsoftware/octobot, PyPI 'octobot') or run from the mobile app; a 2022 CVE cites an older domain, octobot.online, which is not listed. octobot.cloud says the self-custody mobile setup keeps keys on your phone and 'even the OctoBot team cannot access your keys' (vendor claim). CoinCodeCap says exchange keys are 'stored in an encrypted vault' and that OctoBot 'explicitly blocks API keys with withdrawal rights'; we could not confirm either from OctoBot's own docs. Gainium mentions a v2.1.1 fix for 'a security concern' in web-interface redirects; the changelog could not be opened to confirm it. octobot.cloud/privacy could not be fetched.

custody.note: Your coins stay on the exchange you connect, and OctoBot trades through your API keys. For the self-custody mobile app, octobot.cloud says 'your keys never leave your devices' and that 'even the OctoBot team cannot access your keys'. An optional 'personal mini-cloud' is a server you create yourself, 'not a server owned by the OctoBot team'. A self-hosted OctoBot keeps keys in its own config ('It contains exchange API keys...'), so anyone who can reach that machine can reach the keys.

can_move_funds_out.note: Only if your key is limited to what OctoBot's guides ask for: for Binance, 'Enable Reading' and 'Enable Spot & Margin Trading'. OctoBot's guides we could read do not say to disable withdrawals or explain how keys are protected, so a key you create with withdrawal rights could be emptied if the bot's machine or config leaks. Even a trade-only key can place bad trades on your balance.

api_keys.note: OctoBot's Binance guide asks for only two permissions: 'Enable Reading' (to read balances) and 'Enable Spot & Margin Trading' (to place orders). The pages we read give no withdrawal or IP-whitelist guidance. OctoBot's self-custody blog says 'You are responsible of your crypto wallet and API keys security, there is no recovery service if you lose your keys.' The OKX and Bybit setup guides could not be fetched.

incidents.title: CVE-2021-36711: the OctoBot web interface before 0.4.4 allowed remote code execution through mishandled 'Tentacles' (plugin) uploads. Rated critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8, no login needed) in the GitLab advisory, and a public exploit was published (Exploit-DB 50979, 'OctoBot WebInterface 0.4.3 - Remote Code Execution').
incidents.outcome: Fixed in OctoBot 0.4.4; upgrading is the fix. We found no reports of losses.

checks.worst_case: If you self-host OctoBot, anyone who can reach its web interface (no password by default) or the machine it runs on can control your bots and read your exchange keys. A key with withdrawal enabled could then be emptied, and a trade-only key could still place trades that drain your balance. OctoBot says there is no recovery service.
safe_setup: Get OctoBot only from octobot.cloud, github.com/Drakkar-Software/OctoBot or the App Store (id6502774175), keep it updated as OctoBot's blog advises (the 2022 remote-code-execution flaw was fixed in 0.4.4), and start in simulation mode, as the README recommends
Create the exchange API key with only the permissions OctoBot's exchange guide lists (for Binance: Enable Reading and Enable Spot & Margin Trading) and nothing else

If you self-host, turn on the web-interface password (off by default), set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and keep the machine secure and your connection to it encrypted, as OctoBot's web-interface guide and self-custody blog advise

custody.note: Self-custody. Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live) is the companion app; the private keys stay on the Ledger hardware device, 'keeping your private keys offline, far from hackers' reach'. Ledger says it will never ask for your 24-word recovery phrase or PIN.

can_move_funds_out.note: You approve every transaction on the device yourself, to any address. Anyone who gets your 24-word phrase can do the same from another device, and nobody can reverse it.

incidents.title: Users reported implanted Ledger devices bought outside CryptoBilis, including from MediaMarkt in Germany and a store at Singapore's airport. Ledger asked resellers across several Asian markets to halt sales; MediaMarkt Saturn paused Ledger sales. Ledger said the German stock it inspected showed no tampering and it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere.
incidents.outcome: Unconfirmed by Ledger; sales paused at MediaMarkt Saturn and at Asian resellers

incidents.title: Ledger said hardware wallets sold through the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden implants that read the screen during setup, captured the 24-word recovery phrase and sent it out over LTE through an embedded eSIM; attackers then drained funds (drains on October 9, disclosed October 13). Ledger says the implant leaves the Secure Element intact, so tampered devices may still pass its authenticity check, and that all confirmed thefts involve CryptoBilis devices.
incidents.outcome: CryptoBilis paused all Ledger sales and shipments. Ledger says the number of affected devices is limited and asks CryptoBilis buyers not to set up unused devices and to move funds from devices already set up to a new device with a new recovery phrase.

incidents.title: Reported date: a fake 'Ledger Live' macOS app published on Apple's App Store by 'Leva Heal Limited' (not Ledger) stole crypto from about 50 users; three victims lost funds between 2026-04-08 and 2026-04-11 (third-party impersonation, not a breach of Ledger).
incidents.outcome: Apple removed the app 'for malicious bait-and-switch functionality' and terminated the developer account. No reimbursement reported.

incidents.title: Global-e, Ledger's e-commerce partner (merchant of record for some ledger.com orders), told Ledger customers that order data in its systems was accessed without authorization: names, contact details and order details (products, prices). Ledger said its own platform, hardware and software were not breached and that payment data, 24-word phrases and balances were not affected. Scam emails posing as Global-e followed.
incidents.outcome: Customers notified by email from 2026-01-05; number affected not disclosed. No loss of funds reported.

incidents.title: Moonlock (MacPaw) reported four active macOS malware campaigns (Odyssey, AMOS and others) that swap the real Ledger Live app for a fake one showing a fake alert to get the 24-word phrase, then send it to the attackers (third-party report).
incidents.outcome: Security warning; Ledger users told to download only from ledger.com (TechRadar)

incidents.title: Ledger Connect Kit supply-chain attack: a former Ledger employee was phished and their npm account used to publish malicious Connect Kit versions 1.1.5-1.1.7 (first at 08:49 UTC). Dapps that loaded the library (e.g. SushiSwap, Revoke.cash) showed a drainer that tricked users into signing malicious transactions. A fixed version was out within 40 minutes of Ledger being alerted, but CDN caching kept the bad file live for about five hours in total. Ledger says the attacker never had access to its infrastructure, code repository or the dapps themselves.
incidents.amount: ~$600K (Ledger estimate reported by Cointelegraph; The Block reported over $500K)
incidents.outcome: Tether froze the attacker's USDT at 13:55 UTC on Ledger's request and WalletConnect disabled the attacker's project. Ledger committed to make victims whole by the end of February 2024 and to end blind signing.

incidents.title: A fake 'Ledger Live Web3' app on the Microsoft Store drained users' wallets; ZachXBT raised the alarm on 2023-11-05 (third-party impersonation, not a breach of Ledger).
incidents.outcome: Microsoft removed the app the same day

incidents.title: A Ledger customer database was dumped publicly on RaidForums. INCIBE-CERT says it covered about 272,000 customers with email, name, phone number, postal address and product bought. Ledger tweeted the same day that it appeared to be its June 2020 e-commerce database.
incidents.outcome: Ledger warned users of phishing, said 'your assets are safe if your 24-word recovery phrase is', and says it has taken down more than 170 phishing sites since the original breach.

incidents.title: Ledger e-commerce and marketing database breach: a third party accessed it on 2020-06-25. A bug-bounty researcher reported the flaw on 2020-07-14 and Ledger fixed it that day, then disclosed the breach on 2020-07-29. About 1 million email addresses were exposed, and 9,500 customers also had their names, postal addresses, phone numbers or products ordered exposed.
incidents.outcome: Ledger notified France's CNIL on 2020-07-17 and emailed customers. Ledger says payment data, passwords and crypto funds were not affected, and the breach had 'no impact whatsoever' on hardware wallets or Ledger Live. The leaked data later fuelled phishing and physical-mail scams.

collects: Shop orders: your name, email, shipping and billing addresses, phone number, order details and a truncated card number (orders on ledger.com are sold through Global-e, which gets the same data)
Website: IP address, device and browser details and the pages and products you view, if you accept analytics
Ledger Wallet app: device and app details, an equipment ID for each phone or computer, and your signer model and firmware version
Ledger Wallet app: crash logs (kept up to 30 days), plus in-app usage if you turn on 'App Performance' or 'Personalized Experience'
Ledger Wallet app: your public key and balances if you turn on Ledger Sync, and your wallet address if you turn on Transaction Alerts (hashed, then deleted after 7 days)
privacy.can_see: Ledger says it has zero access to your private keys. The app looks up your wallet addresses to show balances and history and Ledger says it doesn't store that, but it keeps wallet addresses that appear in app logs for market analysis for five years after your last connection. Buy, sell and swap partners inside the app handle your data under their own policies.

breaches.summary: Ledger disclosed that an unauthorised party accessed its e-commerce and marketing database on June 25, 2020: about 1 million email addresses, and for 9,500 customers also name, postal address, phone number and ordered products. Ledger says no payment information or passwords were involved and hardware wallets and funds were not affected.

The stolen database was posted publicly on a forum. Ledger says it held about 272,000 customer records with name, postal address and phone number, plus more than 1 million email addresses. Ledger's advice: never share your 24 words with anyone.

checks.worst_case: Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live) is self-custody, so no one can freeze your coins, but anyone who gets your 24 words can empty every account they back up, and that cannot be reversed. Fake 'Ledger Live' apps (Mac App Store, about $9.5M taken in April 2026) and phishing that uses leaked Ledger customer data (2020, January 2026) are built to get those 24 words. Signing a malicious transaction, as in the December 2023 Connect Kit attack, can also drain a wallet.
safe_setup: Download Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live) only through ledger.com: desktop builds come from download.live.ledger.com, and the mobile apps are App Store id1361671700 (seller Ledger SAS) and Google Play com.ledger.live. Ledger's phishing page says fake apps show an 'error' and then ask for your phrase.

Never type your 24-word recovery phrase into a computer, phone, website or app; enter it only on the Ledger device itself. Ledger and its support will never ask for it, so treat any email, letter, call or 'Global-e'/'security' message that does as a scam.
Check every transaction on the device screen before approving, reject any you did not start, and prefer clear signing over blind signing, as Ledger advised after the Connect Kit attack.
checks.status: Oct 13, 2026: Ledger says devices sold by the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis had hidden implants that stole recovery phrases during setup. If you bought from CryptoBilis, don't set up an unused device; if you already did, move your funds to a new device with a new recovery phrase.

incidents.title: An intruder at Brevo, Trezor's newsletter provider, exported 347,149 marketing email contacts and sent Trezor subscribers a fake 'STM32 entropy vulnerability' email asking for wallet backups. Trezor said no Trezor product, wallet or account system was affected.
incidents.outcome: Trezor warned that it never asks for a recovery seed; Brevo confirmed the export.

incidents.title: Customer shipping data leaked through Trezor's fulfilment chain: Metabase told fulfilment partner ShipMonk on 2026-08-06 of unauthorized access, and ShipMonk told Trezor on 2026-08-10. 13,689 customers who ordered between 2026-05-10 and 2026-08-08 were affected: 11,742 had full name, email, phone number and shipping address exposed, and 1,947 had name, city and email exposed (US, UK, Sweden, Colombia, Brazil, Italy, Portugal).
incidents.outcome: Trezor says its own systems and devices were not compromised and warned of phishing by email, phone and letter. No loss of funds reported.

incidents.title: Reported date: attackers abused Trezor's support contact form, opening tickets whose titles were phishing messages. Trezor's automatic reply then came from the real help@trezor.io, carrying lines such as '[URGENT]: vault.trezor.guide - Create a Trezor Vault now...' that led to a page asking for the wallet seed.
incidents.outcome: Trezor warned users on X, repeated that it never asks for the seed, and said it was working on defenses

incidents.title: Unauthorized access to a third-party support ticketing portal used by Trezor (detected 2024-01-17, 20:20 CET). Names or nicknames and email addresses of up to 66,000 people who contacted Trezor Support since December 2021 may have been exposed. The attacker emailed 41 of them asking for their recovery seed.
incidents.outcome: Trezor says no user funds were compromised and no seeds were disclosed. It alerted the 41 users within an hour and emailed everyone potentially affected on 2024-01-20.

incidents.title: Phishing through Trezor's MailChimp-hosted newsletter: MailChimp told Trezor an insider had compromised its service. Emails claiming a 'security incident' urged users to 'Download Latest Version' of Trezor Suite from suite.xn--trzor-o51b[.]com. The fake app (Trezor-Suite-22.4.0-win-x64.exe, built from Suite's source code) asked for the 12 to 24-word recovery phrase and sent it to the attackers.
incidents.outcome: Trezor took the phishing domain offline, paused newsletters, and warned users not to open emails appearing to be from Trezor.

checks.worst_case: Trezor Suite is self-custody, so no one can freeze your coins, but anyone who gets your recovery seed can empty every account it backs up, and that cannot be reversed. Fake Trezor Suite downloads (2022) and phishing built on leaked support and shipping data (2024, 2025, 2026) are designed to get that seed.
safe_setup: Download Trezor Suite only from trezor.io/trezor-suite or github.com/trezor/trezor-suite/releases (mobile: App Store id1631884497 or Google Play io.trezor.suite), and check the desktop installer's GPG signature against the 'SatoshiLabs 2021 Signing Key' (fingerprint EB48 3B26 B078 A4AA 1B6F 425E E21B 6950 A2EC B65C), as Trezor's download guide explains

Never share your recovery seed or make a digital copy of it. Trezor will never contact you about it, so treat any email (even one from help@trezor.io), call, letter or 'vault'/'update' link that asks for it as phishing, and reach support only via trezor.io/support
Verify every address and amount on the Trezor's own screen, not just on your computer, before confirming, as Trezor's scams-and-phishing guide advises

collects: Shop orders: name, shipping address, country, state, phone and email (deleted 90 days after the order; invoices kept 10 years)
Payments: card payments go through a third-party provider; crypto payments keep addresses and transaction IDs for 5 years
Support tickets: name and email, sometimes address and phone (anonymised 90 days after closing)
Newsletter: name and email if you opt in, kept until you unsubscribe
Trezor Suite: anonymous usage data only if you opt in; your data is stored locally or in Suite Sync encrypted backups
Optional referral program: contact details, linked social accounts, IP address, browser and login data, kept with no time limit
privacy.can_see: By default Trezor Suite reads balances and history from Trezor-run servers that Trezor says don't log your activity, and it says your addresses and xpubs are used only in real time; you can point Suite at your own node (also over Tor) instead. Most leaks so far came from Trezor's outside vendors (newsletter, support desk and shipping), and transactions are public on-chain.

breaches.summary: Attackers who phished Mailchimp staff took Trezor's newsletter data: subscriber emails, people who had unsubscribed, and in some cases names and IP addresses. Trezor did not give a count. The list was used for phishing emails pointing to a fake Trezor Suite; Trezor said its devices were not affected.

Unauthorised access to Trezor's third-party support ticketing portal, cut off on January 17, 2024. Names or usernames and email addresses of up to 66,000 people who contacted support since December 2021 may have been exposed; Trezor confirmed 41 cases of misuse and said no funds were affected.

Trezor's shipping provider ShipMonk was breached. Trezor first reported 13,689 customers (orders May 10 to August 8, 2026); on September 4, 2026 it added about 67,000 US customers from 2019-2021 orders that ShipMonk had not deleted, about 80,689 in total. Exposed: name, email, phone, shipping address and order number (some only name, city and email). Trezor said its own systems were not compromised.

An intruder at Brevo, Trezor's newsletter provider, sent a fake 'STM32 entropy vulnerability' email to about 347,000 Trezor subscribers asking for wallet backups; about 2,500 clicked. Brevo confirmed 347,149 marketing email contacts were exported. Trezor said no Trezor product, wallet or account system was affected.

In Perps, your collateral and the borrowed part of the position sit in Jupiter's Perps program against the JLP pool, and Jupiter-run keepers execute trades and limit/TP/SL orders.

can_move_funds_out.note: You sign every send yourself, to any address. Exception: the extension's Auto-Approve is ON by default for jup.ag, vote.jup.ag, lock.jup.ag and verified.jup.ag. Perps trades and limit/TP/SL orders only fill when Jupiter's offchain keepers process them (two run in parallel), and the docs don't say what happens if keepers stop. Ultra Mode sends your signed swap privately for MEV protection, which the docs say lowers MEV risk but doesn't remove it. Jupiter's docs say Jupiter can't recover a lost wallet.

api_keys.note: Jupiter's developer APIs (Swap, Trigger, Recurring, Perps, Lend) take an API key in an x-api-key header from the portal at developers.jup.ag/portal, per Helius's integration guide. A bot still signs every transaction with a wallet key, so that wallet key is what to guard. We found no Jupiter page saying what an API key alone can do.

incidents.title: Fake '$CJUP' airdrop links drained Solana wallets within minutes of connecting. Solana Floor warned users, and Jupiter had announced no airdrop at that time (third-party report). PCrisk listed a similar fake 'Jupiter allocation' drainer, jupag.pro, on 2026-05-21.

incidents.title: Jupiter deleted a post claiming Jupiter Lend's isolated vaults had 'no contagion' risk. COO Kash Dhanda said the claim was 'not a hundred percent correct' and confirmed collateral is rehypothecated. Kamino then blocked Jupiter Lend's migration tool.
incidents.outcome: No user losses reported. Jupiter said it would publish more documentation on the vault design.

incidents.title: Jupiter's main X account (@JupiterExchange) was hijacked and promoted fake memecoins ($MEOW, then $DCOIN). @jup_mobile warned users not to click links or buy promoted tokens. Traders reported losing 'millions' (unverified estimate).
incidents.outcome: Account recovered within hours and posts deleted. Jupiter said 'no funds were ever at risk', customer and treasury assets were in multisig wallets, and the breach was limited to X. Traders' scam losses were not recovered.

checks.worst_case: Jupiter is self-custody, so a leaked recovery phrase, or signing on a fake 'Jupuary'/allocation claim site, can empty your wallet, and Jupiter can't recover it. A Jupiter ID wallet is lost for good if you lose its social login. In the extension, Auto-Approve is on by default for Jupiter's own sites, so a bad transaction there can be signed without you seeing it. Perps up to 250x can be liquidated, and fills depend on keepers Jupiter runs. In 2025 the official X account itself was hijacked to push scam tokens.
safe_setup: Use only jup.ag, and install only from the links in Jupiter's docs: Chrome Web Store ID iledlaeogohbilgbfhmbgkgmpplbfboh (publisher extension@jup.ag), App Store id6484069059, Google Play ag.jup.jupiter.android. Jupiter says any other installer 'claiming to be Jupiter Wallet' is not official. Ignore airdrop or 'claim' links, even from an official-looking X account.

Write your recovery phrase down offline (Jupiter Mobile has no cloud backup). If you use Jupiter ID / Quick Accounts, export the private key on jup.ag and back it up, because losing the social login loses the wallet.

In the extension, open Settings → Preferences → Auto Approve: turn it off, or set a spending limit and notifications, and revoke unused sites under Settings → Security → Connected Apps. Give bots a separate small wallet, and keep larger holdings on a Ledger, Trezor or Keystone, which always ask for confirmation.

custody.note: Raydium describes itself as 'permissionless, non-custodial smart contracts': you trade from your own Solana wallet with no signup and no KYC on Raydium itself. Liquidity you add sits in Raydium's on-chain pools. Every program (AMM v4, CPMM, CLMM, LaunchLab) can be upgraded by a Squads 3/4 multisig with a 24-hour timelock, which can deploy any new code. A separate Treasury 3/5 multisig with no timelock can toggle pool status and change fees on existing pools.

can_move_funds_out.note: You sign every swap and transfer from your own wallet. Raydium says it can't reverse transactions: 'If you sent funds to the wrong address, they're gone unless the recipient voluntarily returns them.'

freeze_policy.note: There are no accounts to freeze, but Raydium's Treasury multisig can toggle a pool's status, and the upgrade multisig can change program code after a 24-hour delay. Raydium lets anyone create pools; Token-2022 tokens with transfer hooks (which can be upgraded after listing and can block withdrawals) are allowed but tagged. LaunchLab 'does not intervene in launches that fail to reach graduation'.

incidents.title: Raydium's legacy AMM V3 program, phased out in 2021 and not reachable from Raydium's app, was drained of about 150,000 RAY, 5,600 SOL and 900,000 USDC from five old pools. Raydium said the cause was insufficient validation of LP mints, which let the attacker bypass proportion checks, not a key compromise. The attacker bridged funds to Ethereum and through Tornado Cash (The Defiant).
incidents.outcome: Raydium said no current users were affected, current programs are under a separate security review, and its treasury will fully reimburse affected LPs. We found no report confirming the payouts.

incidents.title: An attacker took over the AMM v4 pool owner (admin) key and used it to withdraw funds from eight constant-product pools. Raydium said a trojan on the machine holding the key was the likely cause, not a smart-contract bug. CertiK put the loss at about $5.5M.
incidents.outcome: Raydium moved all authority roles to a Squads multisig. LPs were compensated through a Claim Portal (open 2023-01-05 to 2023-04-17), using protocol fees earmarked for RAY buybacks plus team RAY (2,737,521.92 RAY allocated): RAY pairs got 100% of lost principal; other pools got 90% in the original tokens and the rest in RAY plus 20%.

checks.worst_case: You keep your own keys, so a leaked seed phrase, a fake raydium.io clone (some show up above the real site in search ads) or one malicious signature can empty your wallet, and Solana transactions are final. Money in Raydium pools depends on its programs and admin keys: a stolen admin key drained about $4.4M in Dec 2022, a retired program lost $1.34M in Jun 2026, and a 3-of-4 multisig can replace program code after a 24-hour delay.
safe_setup: Open Raydium only from a bookmark of raydium.io, which Raydium says is its only domain; check the address bar character by character, and ignore DMs, because Raydium never messages you first and support never asks for your seed phrase

Use a wallet that simulates transactions and read every signing prompt: reject unexpected transfers, unfamiliar programs or NFT transfers (CLMM positions are NFTs), and paste token mint addresses instead of typing tickers; check mint and freeze authority and Token-2022 transfer hooks before you buy or add liquidity

For more than about $1,000, use a hardware wallet and a separate browser profile, as Raydium's docs advise, and revoke SPL token delegates you don't recognize in your wallet's connected-apps view (revoke.cash does not cover Solana)

custody.note: You sign with your own Ethereum wallet. Deposits sit in Lighter's Ethereum smart contracts, which 'hold the assets and the canonical state root'; the order book and matching run off-chain on Lighter's single operator/sequencer, and each batch is proven with zero-knowledge proofs on Ethereum.

can_move_funds_out.note: Normal 'secure' withdrawals go back to the Ethereum address that created the account. If the sequencer ignores you, you can post a priority (forced) transaction on Ethereum; if it is not processed within 14 days, anyone can trigger the escape hatch ('desert mode'), which freezes the L1 contract and lets users withdraw by submitting a zero-knowledge proof of their balance. The desert-exit circuit was audited by zkSecurity (report dated 2025-11-05, https://reports.zksecurity.xyz/reports/zklighter-desertexit), but L2BEAT notes its source code is not public.

freeze_policy.note: No KYC-style account freeze is described, but Lighter's terms let it 'suspend or terminate your access to the Interface' without notice (https://tostracker.app/document/elliotai-tos). The escape hatch only kicks in after a 14-day forced-transaction deadline, so funds can be stuck for up to two weeks if the operator stops or censors. L2BEAT rates Lighter Stage 0 (May 2026): the team controls the contract upgrade path, and L2BEAT's project page says contracts are instantly upgradable, so a malicious upgrade could steal funds before users exit (https://pr11267-production.previews.l2beat.com/scaling/projects/lighter, preview build).

api_keys.note: Each API key is its own key pair with its own nonce, bound to one account index (master account, sub-account or pool). Indexes 0-3 are reserved for Lighter's web and mobile apps, so bots use 4-254. Registering a key needs an L1 wallet signature (ChangePubKey). An API key can trade, cancel, modify orders, change leverage/margin, manage sub-accounts, make 'secure' withdrawals (only to the account's own L1 address) and same-owner transfers. It cannot, without the L1 wallet signature, transfer to a different owner, make fast withdrawals or approve an integrator with fees. Auth tokens made from the key last at most 8 hours; the docs give no expiry for the API keys themselves. Read-only tokens (1 day to 10 years) can read data but not trade or withdraw, and Lighter recommends them for dashboards and AI agents. Premium/Advanced accounts can mark keys maker-only (post-only orders, modify and cancel only).

checks.worst_case: Your funds sit in Ethereum contracts with a proven state, but one operator runs the exchange: an outage like the 4.5-hour one during the Oct 2025 crash can stop you managing positions, a forced exit only opens after 14 days, ADL can close profitable positions early, and L2BEAT says the team can upgrade the contracts instantly. safe_setup: Run each bot on its own sub-account with its own API key index (4-254), and keep the L1 wallet's private key off the bot server: without it a key cannot send funds to other addresses
Give dashboards, tax tools and AI agents a read-only token instead of an API key, and use separate keys per workload (maker-only keys for market-making bots if your account tier allows)
Only use app.lighter.xyz and x.com/Lighter_xyz (fakes like lihgter-dex.xyz and fake LIT-airdrop accounts exist) and keep only trading margin on Lighter

custody.note: Jumper is a front end: you connect your own wallet and sign each swap or bridge yourself. Jumper's footer links LI.FI's terms, which say 'The LI.FI Smart Contracts operate fully non-custodial' and that the user 'is fully responsible for safeguarding digital assets and cryptographic keys'. To swap an ERC-20 you approve LI.FI's contract (the LI.FI Diamond) to spend that token. LI.FI says finite approvals are the default in its API, SDK and widget, but any infinite approval you gave stays live until you revoke it, and both LI.FI exploits drained exactly those. Bridge legs run through third-party bridges, and LI.FI 'disclaims any liability for such Third-Party Contracts'. Datawallet says 'Customer balances are never held by Jumper' and that Jumper's perps first route to Hyperliquid through builder codes, so perps collateral sits on that venue, not with Jumper.

can_move_funds_out.note: You sign every swap and bridge yourself, and the destination address can be any address you enter. A token approval you gave LI.FI's contract can be used without a new signature from you: in 2022 and 2024, bugs in newly added contract code let attackers pull tokens from wallets with old infinite approvals (153 wallets in 2024). Finite approvals were not affected.

freeze_policy.note: LI.FI can't freeze tokens in your wallet, but it can change and switch off parts of its upgradeable contracts: on 2024-07-16 it 'disabled the vulnerable facet across all chains', and it told users not to use LI.FI-powered apps until then. LI.FI's terms let it 'modify, enhance, or otherwise update' the software, and you agree to 'cease use of the Services' on its reasonable request. You also warrant you are not sanctioned and not a US citizen. Jumper Perps is not available to US persons (Today in DeFi; IQ.wiki). A bridge transfer that stalls depends on the third-party bridge, and LI.FI disclaims liability for those contracts.

incidents.title: LI.FI exploit: GasZipFacet, a contract facet added five days earlier, lacked the call whitelist the other facets use. An attacker made arbitrary calls through it and drained USDC, USDT and DAI from 153 wallets on Ethereum and Arbitrum that had given LI.FI infinite approvals. LI.FI blamed 'an individual human error' in deployment. Jumper (@JumperExchange) told users 'Please do not interact with our platform right now!' and to revoke approvals.
incidents.outcome: LI.FI disabled the facet on all chains the same day and said finite approvals were never at risk. On 2024-07-18 LI.FI said it was working on a voluntary plan to reimburse 100% of affected users with backing from its major investors (Cointelegraph). We found no official notice confirming the payouts were made; Datawallet (2026) says affected users were compensated.

incidents.title: LI.FI exploit (02:51 UTC): the pre-bridge swap feature accepted arbitrary addresses and calldata, so the attacker called transferFrom on token contracts and pulled tokens from 29 wallets with infinite approvals to the LI.FI contract.
incidents.outcome: LI.FI disabled the swap methods, upgraded the contract with a DEX whitelist and made finite approvals the default. All 29 wallets were reimbursed: four were offered conversion into an angel investment, and one partly accepted. The stolen funds stayed with the attacker.

checks.worst_case: Jumper never holds your coins, but every swap needs a token approval to LI.FI's contract. If you ever gave that contract an unlimited approval and it gets a bad upgrade again, as in 2022 and 2024, the attacker can pull those tokens straight from your wallet without you signing anything new. A look-alike site (jumepr.xyz, jymper.xyz, jumper-exchange.org) or a fake 'JUMP claim' or 'xPerps' page can drain whatever you approve or sign there. A bridge transfer can get stuck on a third-party bridge LI.FI takes no liability for, and perps routed to outside venues can be liquidated.

Approve only the exact amount for each swap, never 'unlimited'. Then check revoke.cash (it has a LI.FI exploit checker) and revoke any old LI.FI or Jumper approvals you don't need, especially from before July 2024.
Use a separate hot wallet holding only what you are swapping, bridging or trading right now, and keep long-term holdings on a hardware wallet that never approves LI.FI contracts.

Its processors include AWS, Cloudflare, Namecheap, MongoDB Atlas, Substack, Tally and Google Analytics, and data may go to the USA under EU standard contractual clauses. evidence_grades.B: Reported by the venue from the real account (shown, not ranked yet)

performance_rules.drawdown_gate: Worse than 30% from a peak: shown, not ranked
performance_rules.rank: Sortino ratio, ties on the smaller drawdown
performance_rules.returns: Before the leader's profit share; deposits and withdrawals are not profit

ai_labelled_vaults.rule: The vault's name or the leader's own description on Hyperliquid says it is AI-run. This is the leader's claim, shown with the matching text; TAS does not verify how a vault trades.

hyperliquid_vaults.rules: Open user-led vaults with $1M+ and 90+ days live

ai_agents_with_public_accounts.rule: The agent is registered in an on-chain agent registry, or its operator publishes the trading address on its own site, docs or official account, on a venue with a public account history.

olas_predict.what: Olas Predict trader agents: autonomous AI agents registered in the Olas on-chain service registry, betting on prediction markets from their own Safe wallets.
olas_predict.profit_rule: Trading profit on settled markets: payouts minus stakes and market fees. Leaves out what an agent pays for AI predictions (mech requests) and staking rewards.

leaderboard.disclaimer: Not investment advice. Past results do not predict future results.

rules.source: Hyperliquid's public builder fills, one CSV per builder per day
rules.volume: sum of price x size of fills that carried the app's builder code
rules.realized_pnl: sum of closed PnL on those fills, gross of exchange fees; positions closed through another app are not seen
rules.who: apps whose own site or code says they run AI agents for users; addresses from the app's docs or code or DeFiLlama's open-source adapters

apps.autonomy: autonomous strategies and manual or copy trades
agent trades on request; automated strategies
copilot: AI suggests, the user taps to trade
bots from alerts, webhooks or AI agents, plus a manual terminal
autopilot, AI copilot and manual orders

robot_signals_grade_b.rule: Grade B (venue-reported): MQL5 Signals on real accounts (MQL5's signal rules don't allow demo, contest or cent accounts) with Algo trading >= 90% (MQL5: share of deals made by trading robots or scripts), running 26+ weeks, 10+ subscribers or $10k+ equity. Numbers as shown on each signal's MQL5 page, checked by hand; MQL5's terms forbid automated access, so this list is refreshed by hand, never by a script. Max drawdown is the higher of MQL5's relative drawdowns by balance and by equity.

alpha_arena_recomputed.what: Nof1 Alpha Arena: AI models trading $10,000 of real money each on Hyperliquid, recomputed by TradingAgentStack from Hyperliquid's public fills, funding and candles for every account Nof1 published.
alpha_arena_recomputed.units: return and realized_drawdown are fractions; pnl and fees in US dollars

futureeval.name: Metaculus FutureEval (AI forecasting tournament)
findings: Professional forecasters still beat the best bot team, but the gap was not statistically significant (head-to-head −1.25, 95% CI −4.87 to 2.37).
Among Metaculus's own reference bots, GPT-5.1 (high reasoning) with AskNews search scored best.

usage.what: Usage, not performance: fees users paid and DEX volume (DeFiLlama), and open-source repo health (GitHub, OpenSSF Scorecard).
